model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Budzinski: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, a favorable national environment, and an overwhelming fundraising edge over Wilson. Markets agree, pricing her near 95%, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-implied margin with no evidence warranting a shift.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a surge of outside spending against Budzinski would be the main signal to revisit this.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Nikki Budzinski, the Democratic incumbent in Illinois' 13th District, is seeking a new term against Republican Jeff Wilson. The district carries a Democratic lean of about five points, and the political environment this cycle also favors her party. She has raised nearly $2.9 million and holds $2.6 million in cash, while Wilson has raised about $348,000 with only $12,000 remaining, leaving him little capacity to compete on the airwaves.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put her chances around 95%. The race is rated Safe D, with Budzinski expected to win by a wide but not fully certain margin.
